surprises: The Annual Town Election of 21 May 2022 drew 177 ballots from 8,903 registered voters - about 2% turnout - and every single race was uncontested. Six months later the state election drew 5,335 ballots (59%). Both tally sheets are printed in full in the same report.

Twelve pages (153-164) of the report are the complete reprinted text of the Town's Salary Administration Plan bylaw, printed with additions underlined and deletions struck through. The extract loses that formatting entirely, so from the text alone you cannot tell current bylaw from proposed amendment.
A full 20-grade by 8-step hourly wage grid is printed at p152, as voted. FY2021 prints no such grid, so this is available for one year and not the other.

The Town holds shares of Unitil stock inside two trust bequests ('MABEL ALLEN UNITIL STOCK #20376' and 'JOSEPH HARWOOD UNITIL STOCK', p43) - equity in the local utility, held in nineteenth-century trusts.

The Vital Records page (p140) explains that names were removed at the recommendation of the Registry of Vital Records and the US Department of State, and only counts are now published. That is a documented change of practice, and it is what makes FY2021's missing vitals page (scan failure) impossible to compensate for from this year.
The oldest live capital appropriation on the books is Article 3006 from the August 2002 Annual Town Meeting, 'Development of Cemeteries', still carrying a balance twenty years later (p38).
'Old Primary School Hazardous Abatement' closes FY2022 at NEGATIVE $49,990.00 in the special revenue funds table (p37) - a fund spent into deficit.

The town profile panel (p6) prints TOTAL AREA - 26.63 MILES while the prose four lines below says 'approximately 26.4 square miles'. The report contradicts itself on one page, and the FY2021 report carries the same pair.
The cemetery page's own totals do not add up: 11 full burials plus 32 cremations against a printed Total of 44. FY2021's version has the same defect (37 and 46).

The School Committee 2-year election block is printed twice (pp175 and 176) with the candidate's surname spelled two different ways and identical vote counts - the same race counted once but typeset twice.
A 'TNC Per Ride Assessment Fund' appears in the special revenue funds - the town's share of the state per-trip assessment on Uber and Lyft rides, running at about $400 a year.
ARPA money is visible as CASH: 'Unibank ARPA CLFRF Fund $1,754,181.32' sits in the Treasurer's account list (p40) while never appearing as a revenue line in the receipts summary.
